subject: Traffic-split safety net: SLA exception & rollback policy
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jesse Sullivan <j.sullivan@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Traffic-split safety net: SLA exception & rollback policy

Team / Jesse,

We're preparing the controlled A/B traffic split for the AtlasHealth production route next week (route: /v1/encounter-summarize). Before we proceed we need two things agreed and documented: (1) a temporary SLA exception window for the rollout, and (2) the exact automatic fallback/pinning rules that will be used as our safety net.

Proposal (summary):
- Rollout cadence: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 5 business days (manual step between each bump).
- Pin stable model: redwood-model-v2.3-stable (pinned on route as fallback target).
- Automatic rollback triggers (auto-fallback to pinned model):
  * p95 latency increase of >200ms relative to baseline for 5 consecutive minutes, OR
  * HTTP 5xx spike >0.5% over baseline for a 5m window, OR
  * client-visible error rate (per-tenant) >0.25% for 1m.
- Fallback time objective: rollback routing change applied within 30s of trigger detection.
- Observability: route-level tracing + per-tenant token-level latency budget; we will stream an incident webhook to AtlasHealth monitoring.
- Mitigation economics: If AtlasHealth observes an SLA breach attributable to the rollout during the exception window, Redwood will apply a one-time credit equivalent to 10% of that billing period's usage for the route.

Attachments: proposed-rollout-plan.xlsx (detailed steps), slo-exemption-request.pdf (form).

Please review and ack OR propose edits. Jesse - if you need stronger guarantees (shorter rollback window / higher credit), call it out and we'll respond with feasibility and risk.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Director, Product
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jesse Sullivan <j.sullivan@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Traffic-split safety net: SLA exception & rollback policy

Lauren — quick technical notes from infra/runtime side. TL;DR: plan looks safe with a couple of hardening tweaks.

What we'll implement immediately if approved:
- Canary control loop: automated weight-shift with signal aggregation across replicas. We already support API-level percentage shifts; we'll add a "pin_on_error" guard that forces 100% traffic back to pinned model when triggered.
- Health signals: p95 latency, 5xx rate, and model internal OOM/failure counters. We'll compute a rolling z-score vs baseline to reduce false positives during natural traffic variance.
- Kill-switch: if fallback triggers, all in-flight requests will be allowed to finish; new requests will route to pinned model. Expected propagation to all edge gateways: ~20–30s (30s worst case).
- Graceful pinning: KV-cache migration note — switching back to a different model can cause cold KV misses and ~60–200ms latency for the first few requests. We'll mitigate by pre-warming: spin warm workers using pinned model and run a short prefix-fill pass for high-QPS tenants.

Suggested threshold tweaks (recommended, not required):
- Lower client-visible error threshold to 0.2% for AtlasHealth (they've got tight SLAs).
- Add a 10-minute hold after each bump where we do not progress until all signals are green (safety gate).

I'll attach the small infra checklist to the rollout plan (will add to the XLSX).

—Aditya
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Jesse Sullivan <j.sullivan@atlashealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@atlashealth.com
Date: 2026-11-22T09:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Traffic-split safety net: SLA exception & rollback policy

Lauren / Aditya,

Thanks for the detail. AtlasHealth is OK with a canary provided the automatic fallback is demonstrably fast and that we receive a post-mortem within 24 hours for any incident that impacts our P95 by >150ms. A few asks:

1) Please confirm the exact worst-case user-visible disruption (how many requests could see the increased latency during a rollback event, given the KV-cache cold start you mentioned).
2) We need a signed document that limits our exposure (DocuSign). Can you send the redlined exemption and the credit formula in a signed form?
3) If the fallback occurs and causes measurable customer impact, we expect pro-rated credits applied to our invoice automatically without a long dispute.

If you can confirm above and provide the DocuSign link with the redline, we'll schedule the first bump next Thursday.

—Jesse
Head of Platform Engineering
AtlasHealth

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Jesse Sullivan <j.sullivan@atlashealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T13:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Traffic-split safety net: SLA exception & rollback policy

Jesse — understood. Confirmations and commitments below: 

1) Worst-case user-visible disruption: with pre-warm and prefix-fill, we estimate ~0.5–1.5% of requests for the affected tenant might see an elevated latency (an additional 150–350ms) during the first ~120 requests post-rollback while caches rehydrate. We will flag these in the post-incident report.

2) DocuSign & redline: attaching redlined-exemption.docx for legal review; will create a DocuSign envelope and share link by EOD for signature. The credit formula is documented in the SLO exemption PDF (10% credit of the route billing for the invoiced period for breaches attributable to the rollout).

3) Credit handling: agreed — credits will be applied automatically after we validate the incident against the telemetry and provide the post-mortem (we will not require a separate billing dispute from AtlasHealth).

Operational commitments:
- Auto-fallback propagation target: 30s (we'll state 45s in the DocuSign appendix as a safety SLA for this exception).
- Post-mortem turnaround: 24h.
- One-time trial credit: 10% as noted.

If internal approvals are OK, Ben, can you confirm commercial sign-off and Marissa can you confirm legal sign-off on the redline?

Thanks,
Lauren
